body.estimand_functional: \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), where \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\) is the independently defined Airy value certified by the exact-target face-robust all-count diagonal; the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) has the same second-order value.

sampling_model.design: The causal game permits every outcome-independent assignment law, including arbitrary dependence across labeled units and zero allocation to an arm. Unit permutation reduces any such design to its allocation-count mixture without loss under the permutation-invariant prior; the comparator assigns independently with \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\).
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population of \(n\) labeled units has three fixed binary potential outcomes. Assignment is the sole source of experimental randomness; the Bayes device used for the minimax lower bound is supported on the same finite schedule space and does not turn the causal estimand into a superpopulation mean.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one of three arm labels is assigned to each unit, and the estimator observes every assigned label and corresponding binary outcome.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed. Positive-count exterior allocations are controlled by the exact allocation information gain, while every zero-count face has a target-derivative-one direction with zero revealed-arm score; the resulting Bayes risk is at least \(1/n\) on every proper face.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no estimated superpopulation nuisance. The compact lower prior has longitudinal, transverse, and common-shift coordinates. Exact conditional binary regression and directional integration by parts yield the full-target van Trees numerator; the fixed-parameter diagonal absorbs the explicit \(\varepsilon^{-2}\) prior-score cost before shrinking the transverse width.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The unrestricted two-arm binary minimax risk equals \(n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\) and is attained by Bernoulli randomization with nonlinear shrinkage.
For the two-arm bounded-outcome game, independent assignment remains minimax when estimators are unrestricted.
Under permutation-invariant law classes and linear estimation schemes, complete randomization with Neyman allocation is minimax.
A first-order local asymptotic minimax bound applies across broad sequential experimental designs, including multiple treatments.
Pairwise-independent inclusion attains the sharp bounded-total minimax risk within the class of unbiased estimators.
Limits of experiments yield asymptotically optimal treatment rules under average and minimax risk criteria in smooth models.
Second-order minimax optimality can be characterized through positive solutions of a problem-specific Schrodinger equation.

body.tldr: For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the face-robust three-coordinate prior now yields an exact-target generalized van Trees lower bound uniformly over local, exterior, and zero-count allocations. Combined with a certified rational Airy-feedback remainder for the independent procedure, this proves \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), supplies a computable finite-to-limit modulus, and shows that independent \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) has no second-order loss at this contrast.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent gives only the first-order value and the order of the second-order improvement. The missing point was an all-design lower bridge for the random exact finite-population target, including dependent assignments and allocation faces; applying information bounds only to the conditional mean did not establish that claim.
project_justification.niche: At the fixed unequal contrast \(c^\dagger\), exact binary regression followed by generalized van Trees preserves the target fluctuation and exposes a finite eight-type correction ledger. The basis \([v,d^\dagger,\mathbf1]\) supplies directions that remain informative for the target while being invisible on every proper allocation face.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the exact conditional-regression decomposition, the local Airy cancellation, a uniform positive-count exterior gain using \(H(q)-4\), and a zero-face bound from invisible directions. All remainders are bounded by finite rational maxima and monotone algebraic tests. A separate certified Airy-feedback ledger gives a computable rational primal remainder, yielding a terminating all-future risk certificate.

body.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) and Hull (2026) establish sharp unrestricted results for two arms. The present result is informed by their Airy mechanism but proves a fixed unequal three-arm, full-label, all-design converse with a response-type and allocation-face ledger. Hirano and Porter (2009) and Levit (1986) motivate limiting-decision and spectral arguments; the exact-target conditional regression and finite all-count certificate here are derived directly rather than imported from those smooth-model results. Bai (2023), Armstrong (2022), and Aronow and Lopatto (2026) impose different design or estimator restrictions. Hammer et al. (1996) is only a prospective complete binary-endpoint regimen-trial motivation, not a reanalysis of censored outcomes.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The proof is contrast-specific. Its exterior and face constants come from the explicit eight-type basis for \(c^\dagger\), and the certified Airy majorants are intentionally conservative. The legacy scalar prior remains invalid on zero-count faces, and the finite \(K=3,n=3\) label gap remains only a finite diagnostic. No uniform growing-arm, vanishing-weight, or irrational-contrast statistical limit is derived.
body.honest_scope: The unrestricted sharp equality, equality of the independent and unrestricted second-order values, total finite-data procedures, and a computable finite-to-limit certificate are proved for the fixed rational contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\). For a general fixed permitted contrast, the note retains the proved independent-design Airy expansion and one-sided unrestricted deficit bound, but does not claim that the all-design converse or its modulus transfers by rational approximation. No arbitrary real is assumed computable.
body.interpretation: For a prospective fixed-horizon three-regimen binary trial targeting \(Y(1)-Y(2)/4-3Y(3)/4\), independent assignment with probabilities \(1/2,1/8,3/8\) and the total Airy-feedback estimator attain the unrestricted second-order minimax value. The evaluator returns finite rational lower and upper risk certificates and a computable sample-size threshold for any requested rational accuracy.
